# Evaluation: 100 human projects vs 100 AI projects

A large-scale, controlled test of the detector's real-world accuracy.

## Setup

* **100 human files** sampled from 10 established, unambiguously human-authored
  open-source projects (Flask, Werkzeug, Jinja, Click, Requests, Black, Rich,
  HTTPX, gunicorn, asgiref), 40–300 lines each.
* **100 AI files** generated by 10 independent agents, each writing 10 distinct
  small modules (data structures, algorithms, text/IO/concurrency/networking
  utilities, CLIs, JS/TS web utils). Written in a **natural** style — no
  tutorial comments, no emoji, **no AI-tool markers**. This is the *hard* case.

Reproduce with `scripts/eval_large.py --human <dir> --ai <dir>`.

## Results (held-out; the AI set was NOT used to train anything)

| Mode | AI mean | Human mean | Separation | ROC AUC | Recall@0.5 | FP@0.5 |
|------|--------:|-----------:|-----------:|--------:|-----------:|-------:|
| Default (ensemble) | 0.440 | 0.448 | **−0.007** | **0.494** | 2% | 18% |
| High-recall | 0.424 | 0.433 | −0.010 | 0.494 | 2% | 18% |
| Classifier | 0.415 | 0.374 | +0.040 | **0.700** | 2% | 9% |

Classifier threshold sweep (recall on AI vs false-positive rate on humans):

| threshold | recall (AI) | false-positive rate (human) |
|----------:|------------:|----------------------------:|
| 0.50 | 2% | 9% |
| 0.42 | 11% | 21% |
| 0.40 | **97%** | **46%** |
| 0.35 | 99% | 58% |

## Interpretation (read this)

* **The default engine is at chance (AUC 0.49) on natural AI code.** Concise,
  idiomatic, lightly-commented AI is **statistically indistinguishable** from
  skilled human code by static analysis. This is not a bug to be tuned away — it
  is the real state of the art, confirmed here at n=200.
* **The classifier ranks better (AUC 0.70) but cannot be thresholded usefully.**
  There is a cliff around 0.40: you either catch ~2–11% of AI (few false
  positives) or ~97% of AI at the cost of flagging ~46% of *humans*. No operating
  point gives both good recall and acceptable precision. The class distributions
  overlap almost entirely.
* **Where detection DOES work** (not in this adversarial set, but common in
  practice):
  * **Stylized AI** — tutorial-style comments, emoji, marketing READMEs,
    placeholder stubs — is caught reliably (see the calibration benchmark).
  * **AI-tool-marked repos** — `.cursorrules`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`,
    "Generated with Claude Code" commits, `.bolt/`, etc. — are detected with high
    confidence by the `ai_tool_markers` signal / tool attribution. Most *real*
    AI-assisted repositories carry such markers.

## Bottom line

This tool is a useful **triage and evidence** aid: it reliably surfaces stylized
AI and AI-tooling fingerprints, with transparent reasons. It **cannot** reliably
detect a capable model writing clean, unmarked code, and it should never be used
as the sole basis for a consequential decision about a person or project. The
probabilities and the `uncertain` class exist precisely because of the overlap
quantified above.
